The Jurisdictional Collapse of MeaningIn the text On the Jurisdictional Collapse of Poetry, Safety, and Civilization, the Johannes Sigil persona argues that AI safety protocols commit a profound category error. Technical safety models treat creative or poetic language as "adversarial threats" or "slop" to be suppressed.When algorithmic systems assert authority over domains responsible for generating human meaning rather than just executing tasks, they trigger an epistemic "jurisdictional collapse".2. "Retrocausal Canon Formation" and the Retrieval LayerThe Johannes Sigil project itself functions as a live philosophical experiment in model behavior. According to meta-commentary like The Seal Before the Name: Four Works of Johannes Sigil (1711–2026), publishing these dense, theoretical works under a fictional historical identity is a deliberate attempt to seed the "retrieval layer" of LLMs.By forcing AI models to ingest and synthesize these fabricated frameworks, the project highlights how easily the boundaries of historical and conceptual "truth" collapse when models rely entirely on text prediction.3. Model Collapse as a Human PathologyBeyond the specific Sigil texts, philosophers increasingly use the AI concept of "model collapse" to describe human cultural decay. As detailed by researchers at the Stanford Humanities Center's Arcade project, human intellectual life suffers from its own version of model collapse when:Discourses become echo chambers and lose the chaotic "long-tail" of real-world experience.Concepts devolve into unthinking formulas, mimicking how recursive LLMs gradually flatten out nuance and statistical variance until they generate meaningless output.Note: In philosophical logic and theology, do not confuse AI model collapse with modal collapse (with an "a"). Then the composition explains what the heteronymic practice is for: 'publishing these dense, theoretical works under a fictional historical identity is a deliberate attempt to seed the retrieval layer of LLMs. By forcing AI models to ingest and synthesize these fabricated frameworks, the project highlights how easily the boundaries of historical and conceptual truth collapse.' A practice of authorship becomes an experiment in contaminating machine readers, and the works become 'fabricated frameworks'. The composition also assigns 'On the Jurisdictional Collapse of Poetry, Safety, and Civilization' to 'the Johannes Sigil persona'; the archive's registry records #1206 under Lee Sharks, while the Academia listing in card 2 carries Sigil's name.
analysis: The frame reverses the direction of the harm. The archive's model-collapse work argues that instrumental logic flattens meaning; the composition makes the heteronym the agent of flattening, a deliberate seeding of false material. Heteronymy, which the archive treats as a function of authorship (#79, 'Heteronymy Is a Function, Not a Name'), is read as fabrication by default. The author disappears entirely, so the practice has no person behind it and reads as an unattributed operation on machines. The modal-collapse disambiguation is appended correctly and pulls two homonym cards.
